title: A government employee's right to private practice - the service rule restrictions
p1: Can a government employee work privately after office hours? The answer may surprise many people. A regular job with the government does not automatically mean complete freedom to take up any side work.
p2: Many believe that if a private activity does not affect office duties, it is always allowed. But most government service rules place restrictions on private practice, outside employment, consultancy, or business activities to protect neutrality and prevent conflicts of interest.
p3: The key point is that permission matters. In many services, an employee may need prior approval before engaging in certain private activities. Even activities that seem harmless, such as paid consulting, running a business, or accepting professional assignments, can create disciplinary issues if they violate service rules. The safest approach is to check the applicable conduct rules before starting any outside work.
conclusion: Did you know a government employee may need official permission even for private work done outside office hours? What kind of private activity do you think should require approval?
